ticket.title: chalkline docs check counts test fixture literals as real CLI subcommands, so a repo without a CLI is told to document one
ticket.description:
Reproduced 2026-11-06 while moving miter-inventory into common as gaugeblock-inventory (GB-204). 'chalkline docs check -d common' reported: [DRIFT] Readme - README missing documentation for CLI command 'scaffold'. common has no binary at all. The source of the string is gaugeblock-inventory/src/tests.rs, a clap fixture that writes 'pub enum Commands { Check {..}, Scaffold { path: String } }' into a TempDir: the repo-level clap extractor reads .rs text and treats the fixture as a declared subcommand. Moving the test file from src/ to tests/ did not help, so the scan is repo-wide, not source-dir-scoped. Workaround applied: the fixture now lives in src/fixtures/cli_enum.txt and is loaded with include_str!, so the scan cannot see it; the assertion is unchanged.\n\nRoot cause is the same class as MTR-18, where miter deps counted test fixture strings as real crate references and the fix was to strip literals and comments before scanning. The clap extractor needs the same treatment; every crate whose tests embed a clap sample will otherwise demand documentation for a command it does not have.

FIXED AND VERIFIED 2026-11-10 (common deaa330). Root cause: the inventory scanned every .rs under src, and this suite keeps unit tests in src/tests.rs or <module>_tests.rs, so a clap enum written as a fixture became a real subcommand in the inventory - the literal that accused common of missing documentation for scaffold came from gaugeblock-inventory own test file. Skipped by name, which is the convention the suite actually follows: tests.rs, anything ending _tests.rs, and any tests directory inside the scanned tree; an integration tests directory sits outside src and was never scanned. Proven live with the reinstalled binary, not only in tests: chalkline docs check -d common reports 9 present, 0 missing, 0 drifted where it used to report a missing CLI command for a repository with no binary, and chalkline docs check --workspace still reports 12 targets, 0 drifted, so the fix removes the false positive without hiding a real one. One test writes the same fixture four times - src/cli.rs plus the three test-only shapes - and asserts exactly the two real commands are found.

verification_receipt.command: cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo nextest run --workspace && miter audit --path . --threshold 250 --paths && chalkline docs check -d chalkline
